statement: In controlled-administration studies in adults, a large part of a methamphetamine dose reaches the circulation by non-injection routes, but the published figures depend on what they are measured against. Absolute bioavailability after a single intranasal dose was 79.4% (SD 13.1) in 8 men, measured against a simultaneous intravenous dose of deuterium-labelled drug (Harris et al., 2003). For the smoked route the same study reported 37.4% (SD 14.2) of the amount placed in the device and about 67% of the amount estimated to have left it, while an earlier study in 6 men reported 90.3% of the amount taken up from the device (Cook et al., 1993); the two sets of figures use different denominators and different equipment, so no single bioavailability can be stated for the smoked route. Time to peak plasma concentration was about 2.7 hours (SD 1.2) after the intranasal and 2.5 hours (SD 3.9) after the smoked condition (Harris et al., 2003), and 5.4 to 7.5 hours after a sustained-release oral formulation (Schepers et al., 2003), so it depends on route and on formulation. It is not the time to peak effects: subjective and cardiovascular effects peaked within about 12 to 18 minutes after smoked and intravenous dosing (Cook et al., 1993).
plain: Most of a snorted dose reaches the bloodstream: about four fifths in one study of eight men. For smoking, published figures run from about a third to about nine tenths, because they are measured against different starting amounts and with different equipment, so there is no single number. The amount in the blood peaks a couple of hours after snorting or smoking, and later with a slow-release pill, while the felt and heart-rate effects peak within about a quarter of an hour.
population: Adults given single doses of methamphetamine in controlled-administration studies (8 men in one study, 6 men in another, 8 volunteers in the oral study)
exposure: Single methamphetamine dose by a named route (study conditions: 50 mg intranasal and 40 mg placed in the device for the smoked condition, with a 10 mg intravenous reference; about 30 mg placed in the device with a 15.4–15.5 mg intravenous dose in the earlier study; 10 or 20 mg oral sustained-release)
comparator: An intravenous dose in the same person, given simultaneously or separately, as the reference for absolute bioavailability
outcome: Absolute bioavailability and time to peak plasma concentration by route
magnitude: Intranasal F 79.4% (SD 13.1), n=8. Smoked F 37.4% (SD 14.2) of the dose placed in the device and about 67% of the estimated delivered dose (n=8), against f 0.903 (SE 0.104) of the dose taken up from the device (n=6). tmax 2.66 h (SD 1.16) intranasal and 2.47 h (SD 3.91) smoked; 5.4 h (SD 2.5) and 7.5 h (SD 3.4) after 10 mg and 20 mg oral sustained-release. Peak subjective and cardiovascular effects at about 12–18 minutes after smoked and intravenous dosing.

evidence.extracted: Absolute bioavailability against a simultaneous intravenous dose of deuterium-labelled methamphetamine in 8 men: 79.4% (SD 13.1) for the intranasal condition and 37.4% (SD 14.2) for the smoked condition computed on the amount placed in the device.

Bioavailability of the smoked condition was about 67% when computed on the mean 22.2 mg (SD 8.4) estimated to have left the device, an amount that ranged from 11.3 to 36.4 mg (28%–91%) across the 8 men; the difference from the intranasal route was significant on the nominal doses but not on the estimated delivered doses.

evidence.locator: Results › Smoking Efficiency and Dose (p. 718, continuing on p. 719); Table 1, rows Dose and f (p. 719)
evidence.extracted: In 6 men, bioavailability of the smoked condition was f = 0.903 (SE 0.104) against the dose taken up from the device: participants left 26.9% (SE 1.0) of the material behind and the mean dose taken up was 21.8 mg (SE 0.33) of the hydrochloride salt.

evidence.locator: Table 1, plasma tmax row (p. 125); Discussion, paragraph comparing tmax with other oral formulations (p. 128)
evidence.extracted: With a sustained-release oral formulation the plasma peak came at 5.4 h (SD 2.5) after 10 mg and 7.5 h (SD 3.4) after 20 mg, later than the 2.9 to 3.6 h reported for other oral formulations, so time to peak is a property of the preparation as much as of the route.

Peak subjective effect came at about 18 min (SE 2.1) from the start of the smoked condition and 17.4 min (SE 1.1) after the intravenous dose, and the maximum heart-rate change at 11.8 min (SE 1.6) and 12.6 min (SE 2.8), that is, well before the plasma peak measured for the non-injection routes.

risk_of_bias.note: Both bioavailability studies were unblinded, without placebo and without a described randomization of condition order; the smoked estimate depends on a recovery measurement from the delivery device.

inconsistency.note: The two smoked figures differ mainly because they use different denominators and equipment, which is an explained difference; the statement carries both.

imprecision.note: 8 and 6 participants; the amount leaving the device ranged from 11.3 to 36.4 mg, and the smoked time to peak has an SD larger than its mean.

grade.reasoning: Controlled-administration studies with a within-person intravenous reference start high (METHODS §6.3). Risk of bias −1: neither bioavailability study was blinded or placebo-controlled, order was balanced but not described as randomized, and in Harris et al. (2003) an intravenous dose was infused during each session. Imprecision −1: 8 and 6 participants, and the smoked estimate rests on how much material left the device, which varied by a factor of three between people. Not downgraded for indirectness, because bioavailability by route is measured directly. Not downgraded for inconsistency, because the smoked figures are computed on different denominators; the claim therefore refuses to state a single smoked figure. Strict reading: if the two smoked estimates are treated as inconsistent rather than as explained by their denominators, the smoked part of this claim is very low.
